what_this_is: Which households actually draw an elasticity on the full window, and how the value arm's priced roster cuts them. ONE pass at c066c114b with a PASS-THROUGH recorder on `price_elasticity_for_customer` -- the run is byte-identical to an unpatched one and only the call sites are counted. It exists because `noise_floor` refuses a leg whose side of the cut is empty, and that refusal costs 40 minutes inside a leg; this answers the same question in one pass and names both sides.
confirmed_by: the production path, 2026-09-10T05:02:23Z: the nine-seed `except` leg (longjob-floor-legs-20260910, same commit) refused on seed 11111 with "its 100 roster entries matched none of the 298 elasticity calls this run made" -- the same three figures. An `except` leg with an empty scope re-draws nothing, so its run IS the base-seed run; the agreement checks that this probe patched the same call stream `noise_floor` does, and is NOT evidence about the seeds.
reading: `accounts_that_drew_outside_the_roster: 0` is the whole result. It makes `rest_of_book_sd_gbp` identically zero and `priced_share_of_variance` identically one -- for every seed and at any book size -- so neither is a measurement of where the noise comes from, and the page's `what_would_settle_the_sign` multipliers are exact on this instrument rather than lower bounds.
